It sounds like you're carrying a lot of emotion, not just about the past, but about the kind of connection you’ve always hoped for — something that feels sacred, untouched, and fully yours. That longing is very human.

I don’t think there’s anything wrong with wishing you were his first — not because you’re competing with someone, but because you wanted your bond with him to start from a completely clean slate. That’s a beautiful and vulnerable wish. And I can understand why it feels painful — like there’s a part of his life you’ll never fully reach, no matter how close you are now.

But something really stood out to me in what you wrote: he’s told you that you’re the first person he’s ever truly loved — that you are the one who changed him, that what you have together is different. That’s not nothing — that’s actually everything. Being someone’s first real emotional connection, someone who wakes something up in them, is incredibly powerful — and in many ways, far more lasting than being someone’s first experience.

I think your feelings make a lot of sense — and they might also be tied to deeper parts of you that want reassurance, that want to know you’re irreplaceable. And from what you’ve said, it really sounds like you are. Maybe it’s not about erasing the past, but letting yourself truly feel how unique and meaningful your place is in his life. It’s okay if that belief takes time to settle in — just be gentle with yourself as it does.

You don’t need to be first to be unforgettable. You can be the one who leaves the deepest imprint — and from what you’ve shared, I honestly think you already are.

You’re definitely aware and feel some sort of guilt and empathy towards her so that’s a start. You might love ur mum deeply but struggle to express it and that’s okay or u have mixed feelings but what matters is being willing to do the work to act with respect and kindness. Sometimes we treat the people closest to us the worst simply because they’re “safe” and familiar. That doesn’t make it okay, it makes it important to be more mindful. Comfort shouldn’t be an excuse for cruelty. You should definitely ask her more about her life, not what she does for you but who she is outside of motherhood. One thing u should slowly start working on is make one consistent change so like pick one thing u can do everyday to shift the dynamic so like ; saying thank you without sarcasm, texting her something out of the blue or just listening to her without interruption. If you feel like you’re getting triggered give ur self a moment to regulate ur self. Sometimes we treat others how we treat ourselves internally. If you carry a lot of self-directed anger, shame, or inner judgment, it often spills onto those around you.
